extraction.Name: Eugene Sturdevant
extraction.NOTES: Letter dated February 27, 1918, addressed to Eugene Sturdevant from a member of the House of Representatives (Sixty-Fifth Congress, Committee on Printing). Letter references a query about whether Sturdevant's wife has to accept a patent in fee if tendered under direction of the Secretary of the Interior; states it is the writer's understanding the Secretary has the power to issue the patent any time without regard to whether an application is made. Also references the death of Sturdevant's little son at the school at Mission, with condolences expressed. Letter written on U.S. House of Representatives letterhead; committee members listed: Henry A. Barnhart (Ind., Chairman), Harry L. Gandy (S. Dak.), Edgar R. Kiess (Pa.).
